note: Work: Workers' Rights Act 2019 (Act No. 20 of 2019, Legal Supplement to Government Gazette No. 87 of 23 August 2019), read in the copy the Ministry of Labour publishes: a child is a person under 16 (section 2), and no person shall employ a child for employment or work in any occupation (section 8(1)); a child helping a parent in a family business with a light job outside school hours isn't counted as employed (section 8(2)). No exception for performers is made, so a performer under 16 is held as barred (a reading, not the law's word); the Children's Act 2020's rules, if any, on children in performances weren't read. Section 10 makes a person of 16 or more competent to enter a work agreement and deems them of full age and capacity for it, which the form doesn't hold. Hours and night-work limits for young persons (section 9) aren't held. Majority: not read; the Civil Code's article on minority wasn't reached (no copy was found on a government site today). Service: not read; no Mauritian law on military service was reached.

sources.title: Ministry of Labour, The Workers' Rights Act 2019 (Act No. 20 of 2019)
sources.said: “child” means a person under the age of 16 ... 8. Restriction on employment of children (1) No person shall employ a child for employment or work in any occupation. ... A person who is of the age of 16 or more shall be competent to enter into an agreement and shall, in relation to the agreement and to its enforcement, be deemed to be of full age and capacity.
